part1.tip: A person can be doing several plausible things at once (drinking coffee, listening to music, using a phone) — the correct statement is the one action clearly, unambiguously visible, not merely possible.
part1.tipVn: Một người có thể đang làm nhiều việc hợp lý cùng lúc (uống cà phê, nghe nhạc, dùng điện thoại) — đáp án đúng là hành động được thể hiện rõ ràng, không mơ hồ trong ảnh, chứ không chỉ là điều có thể xảy ra.
part1.tipTh: คนหนึ่งอาจกำลังทำหลายอย่างที่เป็นไปได้พร้อมกัน (ดื่มกาแฟ ฟังเพลง ใช้โทรศัพท์) — คำตอบที่ถูกคือการกระทำที่มองเห็นได้ชัดเจนไม่คลุมเครือ ไม่ใช่แค่สิ่งที่เป็นไปได้
part1.tipZh: 一個人可能同時在做好幾件看似合理的事（喝咖啡、聽音樂、用手機）——正確答案是清楚且明確可見的那個動作，而不僅僅是可能發生的事。
part1.tipFr: Une personne peut faire plusieurs choses plausibles à la fois (boire un café, écouter de la musique, utiliser un téléphone) — la bonne réponse est l'action clairement et sans ambiguïté visible, pas simplement possible.
part1.tipKo: 한 사람이 동시에 여러 그럴듯한 일을 할 수 있습니다(커피를 마시고, 음악을 듣고, 휴대전화를 사용하는 등) — 정답은 명확하고 모호하지 않게 보이는 동작이지, 단지 가능성 있는 동작이 아닙니다.
part1.tipJa: 一人の人が同時にいくつかのもっともらしい行動をしている可能性があります（コーヒーを飲む、音楽を聴く、電話を使うなど）— 正解は単に可能性があるだけでなく、明確に紛れなく見える動作です。
part1.tipId: Seseorang bisa saja melakukan beberapa hal yang masuk akal sekaligus (minum kopi, mendengarkan musik, menggunakan ponsel) — jawaban yang benar adalah tindakan yang terlihat jelas dan tidak ambigu, bukan sekadar mungkin terjadi.
part1.tipEl: Ένα άτομο μπορεί να κάνει πολλά πιθανά πράγματα ταυτόχρονα (να πίνει καφέ, να ακούει μουσική, να χρησιμοποιεί τηλέφωνο) — η σωστή πρόταση είναι η ενέργεια που φαίνεται καθαρά και χωρίς αμφισημία, όχι απλώς πιθανή.
part1.tipEs: Una persona puede estar haciendo varias cosas plausibles a la vez (tomando café, escuchando música, usando el teléfono) — la respuesta correcta es la acción clara e inequívocamente visible, no solo posible.

part1.tip: "Fixing a wheel" and "changing a tire" both involve a bike/car part, but only one matches the specific vehicle and specific action shown — read every noun in the sentence, not just the verb.
part1.tipVn: "Fixing a wheel" và "changing a tire" đều liên quan đến bộ phận xe, nhưng chỉ một đáp án khớp đúng loại phương tiện và hành động cụ thể trong ảnh — hãy đọc từng danh từ trong câu, không chỉ động từ.
part1.tipTh: "Fixing a wheel" กับ "changing a tire" ต่างก็เกี่ยวกับชิ้นส่วนจักรยาน/รถยนต์ แต่มีเพียงคำตอบเดียวที่ตรงกับยานพาหนะและการกระทำเฉพาะที่แสดงในภาพ — อ่านคำนามทุกคำในประโยค ไม่ใช่แค่กริยา
part1.tipZh: "Fixing a wheel" 和 "changing a tire" 都涉及腳踏車/汽車零件，但只有一個選項符合圖中特定的車輛和特定動作——請閱讀句中每個名詞，而不僅是動詞。
part1.tipFr: "Fixing a wheel" et "changing a tire" concernent tous deux une pièce de vélo/voiture, mais un seul correspond au véhicule et à l'action précis montrés — lisez chaque nom de la phrase, pas seulement le verbe.
part1.tipKo: "Fixing a wheel"과 "changing a tire"는 둘 다 자전거/자동차 부품과 관련이 있지만, 사진에 나온 특정 차량과 특정 동작에 맞는 것은 하나뿐입니다 — 동사뿐 아니라 문장의 모든 명사를 읽으세요.
part1.tipJa: "Fixing a wheel" と "changing a tire" はどちらも自転車・車の部品に関係しますが、写真に写る特定の乗り物と特定の動作に一致するのは一つだけです — 動詞だけでなく文中のすべての名詞を読みましょう。
part1.tipId: "Fixing a wheel" dan "changing a tire" sama-sama melibatkan bagian sepeda/mobil, tetapi hanya satu yang cocok dengan kendaraan spesifik dan tindakan spesifik yang ditunjukkan — baca setiap kata benda dalam kalimat, bukan hanya kata kerjanya.
part1.tipEl: Τόσο το "fixing a wheel" όσο και το "changing a tire" αφορούν ένα εξάρτημα ποδηλάτου/αυτοκινήτου, αλλά μόνο ένα ταιριάζει με το συγκεκριμένο όχημα και τη συγκεκριμένη ενέργεια που φαίνεται — διαβάστε κάθε ουσιαστικό στην πρόταση, όχι μόνο το ρήμα.
part1.tipEs: "Fixing a wheel" y "changing a tire" implican una pieza de bicicleta/auto, pero solo una coincide con el vehículo y la acción específica mostrados — lee cada sustantivo de la oración, no solo el verbo.

part1.tipTh: "Adjusting" (การกระทำที่กำลังดำเนินอยู่) กับ "wearing" (สถานะการสวมใส่) อธิบายช่วงเวลาต่างกัน — ตัดสินใจว่าภาพแสดงคนกำลังจัดการกับสิ่งของอย่างจริงจังหรือแค่สวมใส่มันอยู่
part1.tipZh: "Adjusting"（正在進行的動作）與 "wearing"（穿戴的狀態）描述的是不同的時刻——請判斷照片顯示的是人們正在主動操作某物件，還是僅僅戴著它。
part1.tipFr: "Adjusting" (une action en cours) et "wearing" (un état porté) décrivent des moments différents — déterminez si la photo montre des personnes manipulant activement un objet ou le portant simplement.
part1.tipKo: "Adjusting"(진행 중인 동작)과 "wearing"(착용한 상태)은 서로 다른 순간을 묘사합니다 — 사진이 사람들이 물건을 적극적으로 조작하는 모습을 보여주는지, 단순히 착용하고 있는 모습을 보여주는지 판단하세요.

part1.tipId: "Adjusting" (tindakan yang sedang berlangsung) versus "wearing" (keadaan mengenakan) menggambarkan momen yang berbeda — tentukan apakah foto menunjukkan orang sedang aktif menangani suatu benda atau hanya mengenakannya.
part1.tipEl: Το "adjusting" (μια ενέργεια σε εξέλιξη) σε αντίθεση με το "wearing" (μια κατάσταση φορέματος) περιγράφουν διαφορετικές στιγμές — αποφασίστε αν η φωτογραφία δείχνει ανθρώπους να χειρίζονται ενεργά ένα αντικείμενο ή απλώς να το φορούν.

M1: Yeah, we better go soon. I’m so excited! (59) I’ve never seen a Broadway show before. I’ll call John and see if he is ready to go or not.

{W:} (60) Tell him I can pick him up with my car on the way there. Otherwise he had to take the subway and that will take a long time.

[M2:] Yeah, you’re right. I will text him and let him know we are on the way.

M1: Do not text him. I will just call him now and let him know. (61) Oh, and July, I will give you some money for parking because it is quite expensive at the theater.

{W:} 你们都准备好了吗?我们得赶紧出发了，因为演出一小时后就开始了。路上会很堵。

M1: 是啊，我们最好快点走。我太兴奋了！我以前从没看过百老汇的演出。我打电话给John看看他准备好了没有。

{W:} 告诉他我可以顺路开车去接他。不然他就得坐地铁，那会花很长时间。

[M2:] 对，你说得对。我发短信告诉他我们在路上了。

M1: 别给他发短信了。我现在就打电话告诉他。哦对了，July，我会给你一些钱付停车费，因为剧院那边停车挺贵的。

part5.tip: "Have been" is always followed by a past participle (V3) or, less often paired here, another perfect form — never a plain base verb or a present participle used as the main verb.
part5.tipVn: "Have been" luôn theo sau là quá khứ phân từ (V3) — không bao giờ là động từ nguyên mẫu hay hiện tại phân từ đóng vai trò động từ chính.
part5.tipTh: "Have been" ตามด้วย past participle (V3) เสมอ — ไม่ใช่กริยารูปเดิมหรือ present participle ที่ทำหน้าที่เป็นกริยาหลัก
part5.tipZh: "Have been" 後面一定接過去分詞（V3）——絕不接原形動詞或作為主要動詞的現在分詞。
part5.tipFr: "Have been" est toujours suivi d'un participe passé (V3) — jamais d'un verbe de base simple ni d'un participe présent utilisé comme verbe principal.
part5.tipKo: "Have been" 뒤에는 항상 과거분사(V3)가 옵니다 — 동사 원형이나 본동사로 쓰인 현재분사가 오지 않습니다.
part5.tipJa: "Have been" の後には常に過去分詞（V3）が続きます — 動詞の原形や、本動詞として使われる現在分詞は来ません。
part5.tipId: "Have been" selalu diikuti oleh past participle (V3) — bukan kata kerja dasar biasa atau present participle yang berfungsi sebagai kata kerja utama.
part5.tipEl: Το "have been" ακολουθείται πάντα από μετοχή παρελθόντα χρόνου (V3) — ποτέ από απλό βασικό ρήμα ή από μετοχή ενεστώτα που χρησιμοποιείται ως κύριο ρήμα.
part5.tipEs: "Have been" siempre va seguido de un participio pasado (V3) — nunca de un verbo base simple ni de un participio presente usado como verbo principal.

part5.tip: Some nouns collocate with only one specific verb — "a reception is held", not "made" or "done" — so memorize event-related collocations (hold a meeting, hold a reception) as fixed pairs.
part5.tipVn: Một số danh từ chỉ đi cùng đúng một động từ cố định — "a reception is held", không phải "made" hay "done" — hãy ghi nhớ các collocation liên quan đến sự kiện (hold a meeting, hold a reception) như những cặp từ cố định.
part5.tipTh: คำนามบางคำจับคู่ได้กับกริยาเฉพาะเจาะจงเพียงคำเดียว — "a reception is held" ไม่ใช่ "made" หรือ "done" — จงจำ collocation ที่เกี่ยวกับกิจกรรม (hold a meeting, hold a reception) เป็นคู่คำตายตัว
part5.tipZh: 有些名詞只搭配一個特定動詞——"a reception is held"，而不是 "made" 或 "done"——請把與活動相關的搭配（hold a meeting、hold a reception）當作固定詞組來記。
part5.tipFr: Certains noms se combinent avec un seul verbe spécifique — "a reception is held", pas "made" ni "done" — mémorisez donc les collocations liées aux événements (hold a meeting, hold a reception) comme des paires fixes.
part5.tipKo: 일부 명사는 오직 하나의 특정 동사와만 짝을 이룹니다 — "a reception is held"이지 "made"나 "done"이 아닙니다 — 행사 관련 연어(hold a meeting, hold a reception)를 고정된 짝으로 외우세요.
part5.tipJa: 一部の名詞は特定の一つの動詞としか結びつきません — "a reception is held" であって "made" や "done" ではありません — hold a meeting、hold a reception のようなイベント関連のコロケーションを固定ペアとして覚えましょう。
part5.tipId: Beberapa kata benda hanya berkolokasi dengan satu kata kerja tertentu — "a reception is held", bukan "made" atau "done" — jadi hafalkan kolokasi terkait acara (hold a meeting, hold a reception) sebagai pasangan tetap.
part5.tipEl: Ορισμένα ουσιαστικά συνδυάζονται μόνο με ένα συγκεκριμένο ρήμα — "a reception is held", όχι "made" ή "done" — οπότε αποστηθίστε τις συνάφειες που σχετίζονται με εκδηλώσεις (hold a meeting, hold a reception) ως σταθερά ζευγάρια.
part5.tipEs: Algunos sustantivos solo se combinan con un verbo específico — "a reception is held", no "made" ni "done" — así que memoriza las colocaciones relacionadas con eventos (hold a meeting, hold a reception) como pares fijos.

part5.tipKo: 문장에 이미 기간을 나타내는 "for"가 있다면 "during"을 또 추가하지 마세요 — 시간 전치사(along, for, during, over)는 각각 특정 구조에만 맞으므로, 이미 있는 표현과 충돌하는 것은 제외하세요.
part5.tipJa: 文にすでに期間を表す "for" がある場合、さらに "during" を加えてはいけません — 時を表す前置詞（along、for、during、over）はそれぞれ特定の構造にのみ合うため、すでにある語句と矛盾するものは除外しましょう。
part5.tipId: Ketika kalimat sudah mengandung "for" yang menyatakan durasi, jangan tambahkan "during" juga — preposisi waktu (along, for, during, over) masing-masing hanya cocok dengan struktur tertentu, jadi hilangkan yang bertentangan dengan kata yang sudah ada.
part5.tipEl: Όταν μια πρόταση περιέχει ήδη το "for" που εκφράζει διάρκεια, μην προσθέσετε και το "during" — οι χρονικές προθέσεις (along, for, during, over) ταιριάζουν η καθεμία μόνο σε συγκεκριμένες δομές, οπότε απορρίψτε όσες συγκρούονται με λέξεις που υπάρχουν ήδη.

part5.tip: Near-synonym verbs (oppose, postpone, extend) each imply a different action — "postpone a meeting" specifically means delay it to a later time, which is the only one matching a double-booked room.
part5.tipVn: Các động từ gần nghĩa (oppose, postpone, extend) mỗi từ hàm ý một hành động khác nhau — "postpone a meeting" nghĩa cụ thể là dời sang thời gian khác, đây là từ duy nhất khớp với tình huống phòng bị trùng lịch.
part5.tipTh: กริยาใกล้เคียงกัน (oppose, postpone, extend) แต่ละคำสื่อถึงการกระทำต่างกัน — "postpone a meeting" หมายถึงเลื่อนออกไปโดยเฉพาะ ซึ่งเป็นคำเดียวที่ตรงกับสถานการณ์ห้องถูกจองซ้อน
part5.tipZh: 近義動詞（oppose、postpone、extend）各自暗示不同的動作——"postpone a meeting" 特指延後到之後的時間，這是唯一符合房間被重複預訂情境的詞。
part5.tipFr: Des verbes proches en sens (oppose, postpone, extend) impliquent chacun une action différente — "postpone a meeting" signifie spécifiquement le retarder à plus tard, le seul correspondant à une salle réservée en double.
part5.tipKo: 유의어 동사(oppose, postpone, extend)는 각각 다른 동작을 암시합니다 — "postpone a meeting"은 구체적으로 나중으로 미룬다는 뜻으로, 방이 이중 예약된 상황에 맞는 유일한 단어입니다.
part5.tipJa: 類義動詞（oppose、postpone、extend）はそれぞれ異なる動作を示唆します — "postpone a meeting" は具体的に後の時間に延期することを意味し、部屋が二重予約された状況に一致する唯一の語です。
part5.tipId: Kata kerja hampir sinonim (oppose, postpone, extend) masing-masing menyiratkan tindakan berbeda — "postpone a meeting" secara khusus berarti menunda ke waktu yang lebih lambat, satu-satunya yang cocok dengan ruangan yang dipesan ganda.
part5.tipEl: Σχεδόν συνώνυμα ρήματα (oppose, postpone, extend) υπονοούν το καθένα διαφορετική ενέργεια — το "postpone a meeting" σημαίνει συγκεκριμένα να το αναβάλεις για αργότερα, το μόνο που ταιριάζει με μια αίθουσα με διπλή κράτηση.
part5.tipEs: Verbos casi sinónimos (oppose, postpone, extend) implican cada uno una acción distinta — "postpone a meeting" significa específicamente aplazarla para más tarde, el único que coincide con una sala reservada dos veces.

part5.tipTh: คำว่า "than" ที่ปรากฏภายหลังในประโยคเป็นสัญญาณชัดเจนที่สุดว่าช่องว่างต้องการรูปเปรียบเทียบ — สำหรับคำคุณศัพท์ยาว หมายถึง "more + คำคุณศัพท์" ไม่ใช่คำคุณศัพท์เดี่ยวๆ

part5.tipFr: Le mot "than" plus loin dans la phrase est le signal le plus clair que l'espace nécessite une forme comparative — pour les adjectifs longs, cela signifie "more + adjectif", pas l'adjectif seul.
part5.tipKo: 문장 뒤쪽에 나오는 "than"이라는 단어는 빈칸에 비교급이 필요하다는 가장 명확한 신호입니다 — 긴 형용사의 경우 이는 형용사 단독이 아니라 "more + 형용사"를 의미합니다.
part5.tipJa: 文の後ろに出てくる "than" という語は、空欄に比較級が必要であることを示す最も明確な合図です — 長い形容詞の場合、それは形容詞単体ではなく「more + 形容詞」を意味します。
part5.tipId: Kata "than" yang muncul kemudian dalam kalimat adalah sinyal paling jelas bahwa bagian kosong membutuhkan bentuk komparatif — untuk kata sifat panjang, itu berarti "more + kata sifat", bukan kata sifat saja.
part5.tipEl: Η λέξη "than" αργότερα στην πρόταση είναι το σαφέστερο σήμα ότι το κενό χρειάζεται συγκριτική μορφή — για μεγαλύτερα επίθετα, αυτό σημαίνει "more + επίθετο", όχι το επίθετο μόνο του.
part5.tipEs: La palabra "than" más adelante en la oración es la señal más clara de que el espacio necesita una forma comparativa — para adjetivos largos, eso significa "more + adjetivo", no el adjetivo solo.

part5.tip: After a possessive name ("Mr. Allbrecht's"), the blank needs a noun describing a quality of that person — abstract nouns like "promptness" work here, while verbs or adjectives don't fit the slot.
part5.tipVn: Sau tên sở hữu cách ("Mr. Allbrecht's"), chỗ trống cần một danh từ mô tả một phẩm chất của người đó — danh từ trừu tượng như "promptness" phù hợp ở đây, trong khi động từ hay tính từ không phù hợp với vị trí này.
part5.tipTh: หลังชื่อแสดงความเป็นเจ้าของ ("Mr. Allbrecht's") ช่องว่างต้องการคำนามที่บอกคุณสมบัติของบุคคลนั้น — คำนามนามธรรมอย่าง "promptness" ใช้ได้ที่นี่ ในขณะที่กริยาหรือคำคุณศัพท์ไม่เหมาะกับตำแหน่งนี้
part5.tipZh: 在所有格人名（"Mr. Allbrecht's"）之後，空格需要一個描述該人特質的名詞——像 "promptness" 這樣的抽象名詞在此適用，而動詞或形容詞則不適合這個位置。
part5.tipFr: Après un nom possessif ("Mr. Allbrecht's"), l'espace nécessite un nom décrivant une qualité de cette personne — des noms abstraits comme "promptness" conviennent ici, tandis que verbes ou adjectifs ne conviennent pas.
part5.tipKo: 소유격 이름("Mr. Allbrecht's") 뒤의 빈칸은 그 사람의 특성을 묘사하는 명사가 필요합니다 — "promptness" 같은 추상명사가 여기에 적합하며, 동사나 형용사는 이 자리에 맞지 않습니다.
part5.tipJa: 所有格の名前（"Mr. Allbrecht's"）の後の空欄には、その人物の特質を表す名詞が必要です — "promptness" のような抽象名詞がここに適し、動詞や形容詞はこの位置に合いません。
part5.tipId: Setelah nama posesif ("Mr. Allbrecht's"), bagian kosong membutuhkan kata benda yang menggambarkan sifat orang itu — kata benda abstrak seperti "promptness" cocok di sini, sementara kata kerja atau kata sifat tidak cocok di posisi ini.
part5.tipEl: Μετά από ένα κτητικό όνομα ("Mr. Allbrecht's"), το κενό χρειάζεται ουσιαστικό που περιγράφει μια ποιότητα αυτού του ατόμου — αφηρημένα ουσιαστικά όπως το "promptness" ταιριάζουν εδώ, ενώ ρήματα ή επίθετα δεν ταιριάζουν σε αυτή τη θέση.
part5.tipEs: Después de un nombre posesivo ("Mr. Allbrecht's"), el espacio necesita un sustantivo que describa una cualidad de esa persona — sustantivos abstractos como "promptness" funcionan aquí, mientras que verbos o adjetivos no encajan en esa posición.

part5.tip: "Elsewhere" (somewhere else) is a single-word adverb of place that often signals a contrast with a usual location mentioned earlier in the sentence — watch for that "usually X, but sometimes elsewhere" pattern.
part5.tipVn: "Elsewhere" (một nơi khác) là trạng từ chỉ nơi chốn một từ, thường báo hiệu sự tương phản với địa điểm thường lệ đã nêu trước đó trong câu — hãy chú ý mẫu câu "thường thì ở X, nhưng đôi khi lại ở nơi khác".
part5.tipTh: "Elsewhere" (ที่อื่น) เป็นกริยาวิเศษณ์บอกสถานที่คำเดียวที่มักส่งสัญญาณความขัดแย้งกับสถานที่ปกติที่กล่าวถึงก่อนหน้าในประโยค — จับตาดูรูปแบบ "ปกติที่ X แต่บางครั้งที่อื่น"
part5.tipZh: "Elsewhere"（別處）是一個單詞的地點副詞，常常暗示與句子前面提到的常規地點形成對比——留意「通常在X，但有時在別處」這種模式。
part5.tipFr: "Elsewhere" (ailleurs) est un adverbe de lieu en un seul mot qui signale souvent un contraste avec un lieu habituel mentionné plus tôt dans la phrase — repérez ce schéma "habituellement X, mais parfois ailleurs".
part5.tipKo: "Elsewhere"(다른 곳에서)는 문장 앞부분에서 언급된 평소 장소와의 대조를 흔히 나타내는 한 단어짜리 장소 부사입니다 — "보통은 X, 하지만 가끔은 다른 곳에서"라는 패턴을 주의하세요.
part5.tipJa: "Elsewhere"（他の場所で）は、文の前半で述べられた通常の場所との対比をよく示す一語の場所の副詞です — 「普段はXだが、時には他の場所で」というパターンに注意しましょう。
part5.tipId: "Elsewhere" (di tempat lain) adalah kata keterangan tempat satu kata yang sering menandakan kontras dengan lokasi biasa yang disebutkan sebelumnya dalam kalimat — perhatikan pola "biasanya di X, tetapi terkadang di tempat lain" itu.
part5.tipEl: Το "elsewhere" (κάπου αλλού) είναι ένα μονολεκτικό επίρρημα τόπου που συχνά υποδηλώνει αντίθεση με μια συνήθη τοποθεσία που αναφέρθηκε νωρίτερα στην πρόταση — προσέξτε αυτό το μοτίβο "συνήθως στο X, αλλά μερικές φορές αλλού".
part5.tipEs: "Elsewhere" (en otro lugar) es un adverbio de lugar de una sola palabra que a menudo señala un contraste con un lugar habitual mencionado antes en la oración — presta atención a ese patrón de "normalmente en X, pero a veces en otro lugar".

part5.tipTh: หลัง "promise that" อนุประโยคที่ตามมาต้องการสรรพนามประธาน (they, she, he) ไม่ใช่สรรพนามสะท้อน (themselves) หรือสรรพนามแสดงความเป็นเจ้าของ (theirs) เพราะช่องว่างทำหน้าที่เป็นประธานของอนุประโยคนั้นเอง
part5.tipZh: 在 "promise that" 之後，接下來的子句需要主格代名詞（they、she、he），而不是反身代名詞（themselves）或所有格代名詞（theirs），因為空格在該子句中充當主詞。
part5.tipFr: Après "promise that", la proposition suivante nécessite un pronom sujet (they, she, he), pas une forme réfléchie (themselves) ou possessive (theirs), car l'espace agit comme sujet de sa propre proposition.
part5.tipKo: "promise that" 뒤에 오는 절은 재귀형(themselves)이나 소유형(theirs)이 아니라 주격 대명사(they, she, he)가 필요합니다. 빈칸이 그 절 자체의 주어 역할을 하기 때문입니다.
part5.tipJa: "promise that" の後に続く節には、themselves（再帰形）や theirs（所有代名詞）ではなく、主格代名詞（they、she、he）が必要です。空欄がその節自体の主語として機能するためです。
part5.tipId: Setelah "promise that", klausa berikutnya membutuhkan kata ganti subjek (they, she, he), bukan bentuk refleksif (themselves) atau posesif (theirs), karena bagian kosong bertindak sebagai subjek klausanya sendiri.
part5.tipEl: Μετά το "promise that", η επόμενη πρόταση χρειάζεται αντωνυμία υποκειμένου (they, she, he), όχι αναφορική μορφή (themselves) ή κτητική (theirs), αφού το κενό λειτουργεί ως υποκείμενο της δικής του πρότασης.
part5.tipEs: Después de "promise that", la cláusula siguiente necesita un pronombre sujeto (they, she, he), no una forma reflexiva (themselves) ni posesiva (theirs), ya que el espacio actúa como sujeto de su propia cláusula.

part5.tip: Conditional connectors (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) each fit a different logical relationship — "provided that" specifically signals a condition ("if/as long as"), matching a condition-result sentence pair.
part5.tipVn: Các liên từ điều kiện (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) mỗi từ phù hợp với một quan hệ logic khác nhau — "provided that" chỉ rõ điều kiện ("nếu/miễn là"), khớp với cặp câu điều kiện-kết quả.
part5.tipTh: คำเชื่อมเงื่อนไข (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) แต่ละคำเหมาะกับความสัมพันธ์เชิงตรรกะต่างกัน — "provided that" บ่งบอกเงื่อนไขโดยเฉพาะ ("ถ้า/ตราบใดที่") ตรงกับคู่ประโยคเงื่อนไข-ผลลัพธ์
part5.tipZh: 條件連接詞（provided that、in view of、other than、seeing that）各自適合不同的邏輯關係——"provided that" 特指條件（「如果／只要」），符合條件-結果句型。
part5.tipFr: Les connecteurs conditionnels (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) correspondent chacun à une relation logique différente — "provided that" signale spécifiquement une condition ("si/tant que"), correspondant à une paire condition-résultat.
part5.tipKo: 조건 연결어(provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that)는 각각 다른 논리적 관계에 맞습니다 — "provided that"는 특별히 조건("만약/~하는 한")을 나타내며, 조건-결과 문장 쌍에 맞습니다.
part5.tipJa: 条件を表す接続語（provided that、in view of、other than、seeing that）はそれぞれ異なる論理関係に合います — "provided that" は特に条件（「もし／〜する限り」）を示し、条件-結果の文のペアに一致します。
part5.tipId: Konektor kondisional (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) masing-masing cocok dengan hubungan logis yang berbeda — "provided that" secara khusus menandakan syarat ("jika/asalkan"), cocok dengan pasangan kalimat syarat-hasil.
part5.tipEl: Οι δεσμευτικοί σύνδεσμοι (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) ταιριάζουν ο καθένας με διαφορετική λογική σχέση — το "provided that" υποδηλώνει συγκεκριμένα μια προϋπόθεση ("αν/εφόσον"), ταιριάζοντας με ένα ζευγάρι πρότασης προϋπόθεσης-αποτελέσματος.
part5.tipEs: Los conectores condicionales (provided that, in view of, other than, seeing that) encajan cada uno con una relación lógica distinta — "provided that" señala específicamente una condición ("si/siempre que"), coincidiendo con un par de oración condición-resultado.

part5.tip: Adjectives ending in -ing (rewarding) describe a thing that produces a feeling, while adjectives ending in -ed (rewarded) describe a person who receives that feeling — match the suffix to whether the noun is a thing or a person.
part5.tipVn: Tính từ đuôi -ing (rewarding) mô tả một vật tạo ra cảm giác, còn tính từ đuôi -ed (rewarded) mô tả một người nhận cảm giác đó — hãy khớp hậu tố với việc danh từ là vật hay là người.
part5.tipTh: คำคุณศัพท์ลงท้าย -ing (rewarding) อธิบายสิ่งที่ก่อให้เกิดความรู้สึก ส่วนคำคุณศัพท์ลงท้าย -ed (rewarded) อธิบายคนที่ได้รับความรู้สึกนั้น — จับคู่คำลงท้ายกับว่าคำนามเป็นสิ่งของหรือบุคคล
part5.tipZh: 以 -ing 結尾的形容詞（rewarding）描述引發某種感覺的事物，而以 -ed 結尾的形容詞（rewarded）描述接受那種感覺的人——請依照名詞是事物還是人來配對後綴。
part5.tipFr: Les adjectifs en -ing (rewarding) décrivent une chose produisant un sentiment, tandis que ceux en -ed (rewarded) décrivent une personne recevant ce sentiment — faites correspondre le suffixe selon que le nom est une chose ou une personne.
part5.tipKo: -ing로 끝나는 형용사(rewarding)는 감정을 유발하는 사물을 묘사하고, -ed로 끝나는 형용사(rewarded)는 그 감정을 느끼는 사람을 묘사합니다 — 명사가 사물인지 사람인지에 맞춰 접미사를 선택하세요.
part5.tipJa: -ing で終わる形容詞（rewarding）は感情を引き起こす物を表し、-ed で終わる形容詞（rewarded）はその感情を受ける人を表します — 名詞が物か人かによって接尾辞を合わせましょう。
part5.tipId: Kata sifat berakhiran -ing (rewarding) menggambarkan sesuatu yang menimbulkan perasaan, sedangkan kata sifat berakhiran -ed (rewarded) menggambarkan orang yang menerima perasaan itu — cocokkan akhiran dengan apakah kata bendanya adalah benda atau orang.
part5.tipEl: Τα επίθετα που τελειώνουν σε -ing (rewarding) περιγράφουν κάτι που προκαλεί ένα συναίσθημα, ενώ τα επίθετα σε -ed (rewarded) περιγράφουν ένα άτομο που δέχεται αυτό το συναίσθημα — ταιριάξτε το επίθημα ανάλογα με το αν το ουσιαστικό είναι πράγμα ή άτομο.
part5.tipEs: Los adjetivos terminados en -ing (rewarding) describen algo que produce un sentimiento, mientras que los terminados en -ed (rewarded) describen a una persona que recibe ese sentimiento — haz coincidir el sufijo según si el sustantivo es una cosa o una persona.

part5.tipEs: Los cuantificadores (all, most, every, some) parecen todos plausibles pero solo uno coincide con precisión con el alcance que busca la oración — lee con cuidado si la oración implica totalidad o parcialidad.

part5.tip: Prepositions like 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding', and 'without' each require a specific following structure and meaning — "without + noun/V-ing" expresses lacking something, which is the clue for permission-related sentences.
part5.tipVn: Các giới từ như 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding', 'without' mỗi từ đòi hỏi cấu trúc và nghĩa riêng theo sau — "without + danh từ/V-ing" diễn tả sự thiếu vắng điều gì đó, đây là manh mối cho các câu liên quan đến sự cho phép.
part5.tipTh: บุพบทอย่าง 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding', 'without' แต่ละคำต้องการโครงสร้างและความหมายเฉพาะตามมา — "without + คำนาม/V-ing" สื่อถึงการขาดสิ่งใดสิ่งหนึ่ง ซึ่งเป็นเบาะแสสำหรับประโยคเกี่ยวกับการอนุญาต
part5.tipZh: 像 among、unlike、regarding、without 這樣的介詞各自需要特定的後續結構和意義——"without + 名詞/V-ing" 表示缺少某物，這是與許可相關句子的線索。
part5.tipFr: Des prépositions comme 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding' et 'without' nécessitent chacune une structure et un sens spécifiques après elles — "without + nom/V-ing" exprime le manque de quelque chose, indice pour les phrases liées à la permission.
part5.tipKo: 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding', 'without' 같은 전치사는 각각 뒤에 특정 구조와 의미가 필요합니다 — "without + 명사/V-ing"는 무언가가 없다는 것을 표현하며, 이는 허가 관련 문장의 단서입니다.
part5.tipJa: among、unlike、regarding、without のような前置詞はそれぞれ後ろに特定の構造と意味を必要とします — "without + 名詞/V-ing" は何かが欠けていることを表し、許可に関する文のヒントになります。
part5.tipId: Preposisi seperti 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding', dan 'without' masing-masing memerlukan struktur dan makna tertentu setelahnya — "without + kata benda/V-ing" mengungkapkan tidak adanya sesuatu, yang menjadi petunjuk untuk kalimat terkait izin.
part5.tipEl: Προθέσεις όπως 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding' και 'without' απαιτούν η καθεμία συγκεκριμένη δομή και σημασία μετά από αυτές — το "without + ουσιαστικό/V-ing" εκφράζει την έλλειψη κάτι, που είναι η ένδειξη για προτάσεις σχετικές με άδεια.
part5.tipEs: Preposiciones como 'among', 'unlike', 'regarding' y 'without' requieren cada una una estructura y significado específicos después — "without + sustantivo/V-ing" expresa la carencia de algo, la pista para oraciones relacionadas con permisos.

part5.tip: A past participle used as an adjective ("decorated") can still be modified by an adverb describing manner — "cheerfully decorated" tells us how the decorating was done, not just that it happened.
part5.tipVn: Quá khứ phân từ dùng như tính từ ("decorated") vẫn có thể được bổ nghĩa bởi trạng từ chỉ cách thức — "cheerfully decorated" cho biết việc trang trí được thực hiện như thế nào, không chỉ là việc nó đã xảy ra.
part5.tipTh: past participle ที่ใช้เป็นคำคุณศัพท์ ("decorated") ยังคงถูกขยายด้วยกริยาวิเศษณ์บอกลักษณะได้ — "cheerfully decorated" บอกว่าการตกแต่งทำอย่างไร ไม่ใช่แค่ว่ามันเกิดขึ้น
part5.tipZh: 作為形容詞使用的過去分詞（"decorated"）仍可被表示方式的副詞修飾——"cheerfully decorated" 告訴我們裝飾是如何完成的，而不僅僅是它發生了。
part5.tipFr: Un participe passé utilisé comme adjectif ("decorated") peut toujours être modifié par un adverbe de manière — "cheerfully decorated" nous dit comment la décoration a été faite, pas seulement qu'elle a eu lieu.
part5.tipKo: 형용사로 쓰인 과거분사("decorated")도 방식을 나타내는 부사로 수식될 수 있습니다 — "cheerfully decorated"는 장식이 어떻게 되었는지를 알려주지, 단지 일어났다는 사실만을 알려주지 않습니다.
part5.tipJa: 形容詞として使われる過去分詞（"decorated"）は様態を表す副詞で修飾できます — "cheerfully decorated" は装飾がどのように行われたかを伝えるもので、単に起こったことだけを伝えるのではありません。
part5.tipId: Past participle yang digunakan sebagai kata sifat ("decorated") masih bisa dimodifikasi oleh kata keterangan yang menggambarkan cara — "cheerfully decorated" memberi tahu kita bagaimana dekorasi dilakukan, bukan hanya bahwa itu terjadi.
part5.tipEl: Μια μετοχή παρελθόντα χρόνου που χρησιμοποιείται ως επίθετο ("decorated") μπορεί ακόμα να τροποποιηθεί από ένα επίρρημα τρόπου — το "cheerfully decorated" μας λέει πώς έγινε η διακόσμηση, όχι απλώς ότι συνέβη.
part5.tipEs: Un participio pasado usado como adjetivo ("decorated") aún puede ser modificado por un adverbio de modo — "cheerfully decorated" nos dice cómo se hizo la decoración, no solo que ocurrió.

part5.tipTh: คำนามใกล้เคียงกัน (component, degree, requirement, impact) แต่ละคำมี collocation ตายตัวของตัวเอง — "have an impact on something" คือคู่คำตามธรรมชาติ ควรเรียนรู้ทั้งวลีแทนที่จะเรียนแค่คำเดียว

part5.tipFr: Des noms proches en sens (component, degree, requirement, impact) ont chacun leur propre collocation fixe — "have an impact on something" est l'association naturelle, apprenez donc la phrase entière plutôt que le mot seul.

part5.tipJa: 類義名詞（component、degree、requirement、impact）はそれぞれ固有の決まった連語を持ちます — "have an impact on something" が自然な組み合わせなので、単語だけでなく句全体を学びましょう。
part5.tipId: Kata benda hampir sinonim (component, degree, requirement, impact) masing-masing memiliki kolokasi tetapnya sendiri — "have an impact on something" adalah pasangan alami, jadi pelajari keseluruhan frasa daripada kata itu sendiri.

'And' + adv + 'so': frase adverbial que modifica la parte anterior de la oración
part5.tip: A fixed phrase like "and reasonably so" acts as an adverb modifying the whole previous clause, confirming that an action (raising rent) was done justifiably — recognize such phrases as set expressions, not word-by-word grammar.
part5.tipVn: Một cụm từ cố định như "and reasonably so" đóng vai trò trạng từ bổ nghĩa cho toàn bộ mệnh đề trước đó, xác nhận một hành động (tăng tiền thuê) được thực hiện một cách hợp lý — hãy nhận diện các cụm này như thành ngữ cố định, không phân tích ngữ pháp từng từ.

part5.tipId: Frasa tetap seperti "and reasonably so" berfungsi sebagai kata keterangan yang memodifikasi seluruh klausa sebelumnya, menegaskan bahwa suatu tindakan (menaikkan sewa) dilakukan secara wajar — kenali frasa semacam itu sebagai ungkapan tetap, bukan tata bahasa kata demi kata.

part6.hint:
143 - have been chosen
Need a passive verb form ("to be chosen").

144 - position
Fixed phrase: "apply for a position".

145 - We would like you to come in at 1:00 P.M.
The previous sentence gives the interview time range (1:00-6:00 P.M.); this sentence connects to the following one about the location. Sentence A is unrelated, C is unrelated (interviewers asking questions), and D is redundant since a specific schedule was already given.

146 - qualify
Enable = make possible; approve = to agree to; refuse = to decline; qualify = to meet requirements — "qualify" fits the meaning best (whether you meet the requirements).

part7.description:
MEMO

To: All staff
From: Elizabeth Paine
Date: January 24
Subject: Sick Leave

Attention employees.

We are going to make adjustments to our policies concerning sick leave here at Zimnet Corporation, We are considering reducing the number of paid vacation days and instead increasing the number of paid sick days available to employees. Before we make any changes, we would like to gather the opinions of employees on this matter. Please e-mail Tony Nugent at tonynugent@zimnet.com. He will be collecting and analyzing your responses. Afterward, Management will produce a corresponding policy proposal by February 24. Once the proposal has been made, a meeting will be called to discuss its implementation among all of our employees. I hope this process can be helpful to all of our employees, and please be active in your participation

Sincerely,
Elizabeth Paine

Penny Jones3:27
I just got a call from Martin that his client Mr. Patrick would like to have his order two weeks earlier than originally planned. So, by next week Monday essentially. Do you think this is possible? I'd like your input.
Karen Norman3:28
There's no problem on our end. Most of the leather has already been cut. We've already sent many of the pieces to be sewn. The rest of the work should take a couple of hours
Neil Park3:29
The handles are complete and about half the bags are near completion. I'll get them to Lauren soon. I think we should be able to finish sewing the bags by tomorrow evening.
Penny Jones3:30
I'm glad to hear that most of the handbags are almost finished. Lauren, how long will it take to get the hardware attached or sewn in?
Lauren Nichols3:31
We're currently working on the Jenk and Cenk twin's orders...
Penny Jones3:32
We have more than enough time to complete the twin's orders so I can authorize your workers to put aside that project for now. How long will Mr. Patrick's order take?
Lauren Nichols3:33
The zippers need to be sewn in but the studs will be glued, which makes the work easier. I think we need about a day.
Kevin Harding3:34
It'll take us only a couple of hours to have the order packaged safely to be shipped.
Penny Jones3:35
Thank you so much. I'll let our client know.

part7.description:
Travel & Recreation
123 Gllmoew Street
Orange County, CA 48857

November 15
Mr. Peter Kang
3820 Rivervalley Heights
Seattle, WA 19387

Dear Mr. Kang,

We at Travel & Recreation thank you for your subscription to our magazine. As you have been a long time subscriber, I am excited to inform you about our new subscription plan for our VIP members. -[1]- As a member, you will continue to receive monthly editions of our magazine and access to our new online e-magazine services. You can simply download a digital version of the print magazine to any mobile device at no extra cost. -[2]- Furthermore, you can access background information about our authors, journalists, and guest writers, as well as detailed information about the locations and places that are covered in the magazine. In addition, you can access the recipes to the most popular restaurants around the world and, most exciting of all, we will hold an exclusive competition for our VIP members with a chance to win a trip for two to Hawai. -[3]- Our regular subcribers, as well as VIP members, will have a chance to win a dining experience at 5-star restaurant Bellisimo.

Again we thank you for your continued support and we hope you enjoy the many changes we have made to our services as we strive to entertain and educate our loyal subscribers. -[4]- Please fill out the application form that is attached to this letter. Please check which subscription plan you wish to join. If you send in a $100 fee, you will receive the regular subscription plan. If you send in a $200 fee, you will become a VIP member.

We appreciate your support and hope to hear from you soon.
Sincerely,
Victoria Adams

Next Month at the BeLmont Historical Society

Documentary Film Night: "Exploring the Arctic"
May 5, Spruce Theater

Photo Exhibition: "America in the 20th Century"
Opening Night, May 9, Linda Cameron Art Gallery

AuthorTalk: Glen Campbell, "The Culture of Early America"
May 14, Chris Charlton Auditorium

Musical Performance: "American Folk Masters"
May 22, Spruce Theater

Children and seniors are allowed free entry to all events. Additionally, if you pay the registration fee and become a member of the Beimont Historical Society on our website, you can attend any event free of charge.

For questions about booking group visits, contact David Smith at dsmith@belmonthistoricaisociety.com For more details regarding upcoming events and venue locations, or to rent one of our venues, visit us at www.belmonthistoricalsociety.com.
To: David Smith <dsmith@belmonthistoricalsociety.com>
From: Jared Tate <jtate@clarkuniversity.com>
Date: April 22
Subject: Group Visit
Dear Mr. Smith,

Hello, my name is Jared Tate and I am a professor in the History Department at Clark . University in downtown Maryville.

I am teaching an introductory history course for freshmen this semester, and I thought it would be helpful to attend the event featurin.g Mr. Campbell. His talk is very pertinent to the subjects we are currently covering in class.

I was also wondering if it would be possible to arrange a question-and answer session between Mr. Campbell and my group of about 50 students. Please tell him that we are looking forward to seeing him.

I appreciate your reading my e-mail and I hope to hear back from you soon.

Jared Tate
History Department, Clark University

Date and TimeEventLocationAdditional Notes

To: Richard White <rwhite@newtonlibrary.edu>
From: Linda Carter <lcarter121 @seprus.com>
Date: April 1
Subject: Beginner English Conversation Club
Hi Mr. White,

My name is Linda Carter and I am the instructor for the Beginner English Conversation Club to be held on April ro. I noticed that the library recently built the Media Lab with funds raised by library patrons. I was hoping to change classrooms in order to use my new educational resources by integrating computers into my English conversation class. Could you please reschedule my class to be provided in the same classroom as Never Too Late to Learn instead of the Education Center? I think my students will appreciate the practical English skills they can learn on computers. Also, could you please send an e-mail to all of the students who have signed up for the class? They will need to be informed about the room change.

Thank you in advance for your assistance,
Linda Carter
To: Richard White <rwhite@newtonlibrary.edu>
From: Linda Carter <lcarter121 @seprus.com>
Date: April 2
Subject: Room Change
Dear Ms. Carter,

I would be happy to move your Beginners English Conversation course to the classroom with the updated media lab; for your reference, this is room 3A. Unfortunately, I do not have the emails for all of the students who signed up for your course. Many students only provided their names. I could post a sign at the entrance to the library advertising your course and make a note of the room change, if that would be acceptable for you. Please let me know if you would like me to do this.

Thank you and all the best,
Richard White
Library Projects Coordinator

To: Tony Walker <twalker@icmcorp.com>
From: Suzie Mason <smason@icmcorp.com>
Date: May 4
Subject: Summer Calendar
Attachment: budget.doc
Dear Mr. Walker,

Iam finalizing the calendar of summer events for our company. Because we went over budget last year on employee appreciation events, I think it would be wise to find more affordable recreational activities. Attached is a breakdown of projected expenses for summer events that I have planned.

July 6: Anchorage Flower Festtival
July 22: Art in the Park at Lawrence Park
August 6: Bicycle Tours of the Anchorage Countryside
August 19: FHlorrseback Riding at Sweet Meadow Ranch

I have scheduled fewer outdoor activities this year compared to last year. This year I would like to take advantage of a new outdoor recreational opportunity that I read about on the Anchorage Reporter website. You can read the article by clicking on this link: www.anchoragereporterr.com/new_trails

Please let me know your opinion,
Suzie Mason
Human Resources Manager
Anchorage Reporter
Bike Tours of the Anchorage Countryside to Start August 6

May 2—The Anchorage Bike Club will be hosting an annual bike riding event this summer, beginning on August 6 and running through August 7. The event will start at 10:00 A.M. on both days at the Anchorage Community Center, If you are driving a vehicle to the starting point, it would be better to use the parking lot behind the community center.

Anchorage Bike Club President Jean Frost stated, "The xides will range from 5 to 20 miles and will take bikers through scenic areas in Anchorage, Overall, the bike tours will go ahead at a leisurely pace so that bikers of all skill levels can participate. However, local bikers with ample experience might lead a faster-paced group."

Bikers in the tours will learn about riding techniques, bicycle maintenance, and proper nutrition half an hour before the event starts. AU participants must have biking helmets on. They are also encouraged to bring their own water to prevent dehydration while biking.
BICYCLE TOUR SIGN-UP SHEET

If you intend to participate in the August 6 bicycle tour, please write down your name, department, and level of experience or fittness. If we have enough people sign up as advanced, we can coordinate two separate tours. If there are not enough for two tours, we would like to encourage all riders to stay together so that everyone can join in the team building exercises we have planned. Thank you for your participation and we look forward to seeing everyone at the event!

Sally JenkinsInventoryBeginner

All returns must be sent back to Four Seasons Apparel Outlet within 7 days of delivery. They can be exchanged for a different item or returned for a refund. If you choose a refund, we will credit the card used for purchase.

Phone: 432-555-6729

I ordered a medium-sized Snowy SChristmas Sweafter from your online store on April 22, but I mistakenly received a small-sized one. I would like to exchange it for the correct one.
From: Debra Clarke <debraclarke@fourseasons.com>
To: Sally Nelson <snelson@clandon.net>

Subject: Exchange
Dear Ms. Nelson,

We have received your request to exchange the sweater you purchased. We sincerely apologize for this mistake. We shipped the correct item immediately as per your request. Your shipment can be tracked on our website using the following tracking number: 447H57J.

Because this was our mistake, we have returned $7 to your credit card in order to reimburse you for the return shipping costs. Please check your balance to confirm this.

If you experience any future problems with this order, you may call me at 303-555-4387. I will help you solve any problem that may arise.

Debra Clarke
To: Sally Nelson <snelson@clandon.net>
From: Debra Clarke <debraclarke@fourseasons.com>
Date: May 4
Subject: Return Error
Dear Ms. Clarke,

I was glad to receive your email regarding my return and am thankful that Four Seasons was thoughtful enough to refund my shipping cost.

That being said, I checked my account and have received the promised refund. Additionally, the new sweater that was sent to me was the right size, but I had ordered the Snowy Christmas design. Sally Nelson
